translations.idiomatic: (Note: the text below is missing.)〉

sentences.zh: 為鄆州節度判官。

translations.literal: He served as military governor adjutant of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as adjutant to the military governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗聞鳳名，得之甚喜，以為護鑾學士。

translations.literal: Tang Zhuangzong heard Feng's name and was greatly pleased to obtain him, appointing him Guardian of the Imperial Carriage Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong of Tang heard Feng's reputation, he was delighted to obtain him and appointed him guardian-of-the-carriage academician.

sentences.zh: 後莊宗即位，拜鳳中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later when Zhuangzong took the throne, Feng was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Zhuangzong took the throne, Feng was appointed secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 及入汴，改授禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When they entered Bian, he was changed to Outside Regular of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the court entered Bian, he was reassigned as outside regular of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 莊宗及劉皇后幸張全義第，後奏曰：「妾五六歲失父母，每見老者，思念尊親泣下，以全義年德，妾欲父事之，以慰孤女之心。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited Zhang Quanyi's residence. The empress memorialized: "Your concubine lost her parents at five or six. Whenever I see the elderly I weep remembering my elders. Given Quanyi's age and virtue, your concubine wishes to treat him as a father to comfort this orphaned girl's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited Zhang Quanyi's residence. The empress said, "Your concubine lost her parents at five or six. Whenever I see the elderly I weep for my lost kin. Given Quanyi's age and virtue, I wish to treat him as a father to comfort this orphaned girl's heart.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗許之，命鳳作箋上全義，定往來儀注。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong assented and ordered Feng to compose a document to Quanyi and fix the ritual forms for their intercourse.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong agreed and ordered Feng to draft a letter to Quanyi and fix the ritual forms for their exchanges.

sentences.zh: 鳳上書極諫，不納。

translations.literal: Feng submitted a memorial of strong remonstrance; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Feng submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance, but it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 天成初，置端明殿學士，鳳與馮道俱任其職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng the Duanming Hall academicians were established; Feng and Feng Dao both held the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng era the Duanming Hall academicians were established, and Feng and Feng Dao both held the post.

sentences.zh: 時任圜為宰相，為安重誨所傾，以至罷相歸磁州。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Huan was chief minister and was undermined by An Chonghui until he was dismissed and returned to Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ren Huan was chief minister but was undermined by An Chonghui until he was dismissed and sent home to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 及朱守殷以汴州叛，馳驛賜圜自盡。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou, an express order granted Huan suicide.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou, an express order commanded Huan to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 既而鳳哭謂安重誨曰：「任圜，義士也，肯造逆謀以讎君父乎？

translations.literal: Then Feng weeping said to An Chonghui: "Ren Huan is a man of righteousness. Would he contrive rebellion to avenge himself on ruler and father?
translations.idiomatic: Then Feng wept and said to An Chonghui, "Ren Huan is a man of righteousness. Would he contrive rebellion to strike at his ruler and father?

sentences.zh: 如此濫刑，何以安國！

translations.literal: With such indiscriminate punishment, how can the state be secure!
translations.idiomatic: With such indiscriminate punishment, how can the state be secure!

sentences.zh: 」重誨笑而不責。

translations.literal: " Chonghui smiled and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: " Chonghui smiled and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 是冬，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: That winter he acted as commissioner for the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he served as acting commissioner for the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年春，有僧自西國取經回，得佛牙大如拳，褐漬皴裂，進於明宗。

translations.literal: The next spring a monk returned from the western regions with sutras, obtaining a Buddha tooth as large as a fist, brown-stained and cracked, which he presented to Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring a monk returned from the western regions with sutras, bringing a Buddha tooth as large as a fist, brown-stained and cracked, which he presented to Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 鳳揚言曰：「 曾聞佛牙錘鍛不壞，請試之。

translations.literal: Feng proclaimed: "I have heard that Buddha teeth cannot be destroyed by hammering and forging. Please test it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng declared publicly, "I have heard that Buddha teeth cannot be destroyed by hammering and forging. Let us test it.

sentences.zh: 」隨斧而碎。

translations.literal: " It shattered at the stroke of the axe.
translations.idiomatic: " It shattered at the stroke of the axe.

sentences.zh: 時宮中所施已逾數千緡，聞毀乃止。

translations.literal: The palace had already spent several thousand strings of cash on it; hearing of the destruction they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The palace had already spent several thousand strings of cash on it; when they heard it was destroyed, they stopped.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還洛，留知汴州事，尋授中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, Feng was left to manage Bianzhou affairs; soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, Feng was left to manage affairs at Bianzhou; soon he was appointed vice director of the secretariat and grand councilor.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （李之儀《姑溪居士集》：鳳為《莊宗實錄》，將何挺論劉煦疏不載，句既相，遂引鳳共政事。）〉

translations.literal: (Li Zhiyi's 《Guxi Jushi Ji》: Feng compiled the 《Veritable Records of Zhuangzong》. He did not record He Ting's discussion of Liu Xu's memorial. Once Ju had become chief minister, he brought Feng in to share government.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Li Zhiyi's 《Collected Works of the Hermit of Guxi》: Feng compiled the 《Veritable Records of Zhuangzong》 and omitted He Ting's discussion of Liu Xu's memorial. Once Ju became chief minister, he brought Feng in to share government.)〉

sentences.zh: 長興中，安重誨出鎮河中，人無敢言者，惟鳳極言於上前曰：「重誨是陛下家臣，其心終不背主，五年秉權，賢豪俯伏，但不周防，自貽浸潤。

translations.literal: In Changxing, An Chonghui went out to govern Hezhong. No one dared speak; only Feng spoke strongly before the throne: "Chonghui is Your Majesty's household servant; in his heart he will never turn against his lord. For five years he held power and worthy men bowed low, but through lack of precaution he brought slander upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era, An Chonghui went out to govern Hezhong. No one dared speak up; only Feng spoke forcefully before the throne: "Chonghui is Your Majesty's household servant and in his heart will never turn against his lord. For five years he held power and worthy men bowed before him, but through lack of precaution he brought slander upon himself.

sentences.zh: 」明宗以為朋黨，不悅其奏。

translations.literal: " Mingzong thought it factional and was displeased with the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong took this for factional pleading and was displeased with the memorial.

sentences.zh: 重誨獲罪，乃出邢州節度使。

translations.literal: Chonghui was punished and then sent out as military governor of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui was punished and then sent out as military governor of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及閔帝蒙塵於衛州，鳳集賓佐軍校，垂涕曰：「主上播遷，渡河而北，吾輩安坐不赴奔問，於禮可乎？

translations.literal: When Emperor Min was driven from the capital at Weizhou, Feng gathered guests, staff, and military officers and said with tears: "Our lord is in exile, crossing the river north. Can we sit at ease and not hurry to offer aid? By ritual is this permissible?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min was driven into exile at Weizhou, Feng gathered his guests, staff, and military officers and said through tears, "Our lord is in exile, crossing the river to the north. Can we sit at ease and not hurry to offer aid? Is that permissible by ritual?

sentences.zh: 」軍校曰：「唯公所使。

translations.literal: " The officers said: "We await only your command.
translations.idiomatic: " The officers said, "We await only your command.

sentences.zh: 」將行，聞閔帝遇弑而止。

translations.literal: " As they were about to depart, they heard that Emperor Min had been assassinated and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " As they were about to set out, they heard that Emperor Min had been assassinated and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，召還，授太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was summoned back and appointed Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he was summoned back and appointed grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 既而病足，不能朝謁。

translations.literal: Soon he had crippled feet and could not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his feet failed him and he could no longer attend court.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，自為蓍筮，卦成，投蓍而歎曰：「吾家世無五十者，而復窮賤；

translations.literal: Seriously ill, he divined for himself with yarrow stalks. When the hexagram was complete he cast the stalks and sighed: "In my family none has lived past fifty, and moreover in poverty and low station;
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew grave, he divined for himself with yarrow stalks. When the hexagram was complete he cast the stalks aside and sighed, "In my family no one has lived past fifty, and all have been poor and lowly;

sentences.zh: 吾年已五十，又為將相，豈有遐壽哉！

translations.literal: I am already fifty and have been general and chief minister—can there be long life!
translations.idiomatic: I am already fifty and have been a general and chief minister—how can there be long life!

sentences.zh: 」清泰二年三月卒。

translations.literal: " In the third month of the second year of Qingtai he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the third month of the second year of Qingtai.

sentences.zh: 鳳性豁達，輕財重義，凡士友以窮厄告者，必傾其資而餉之，人士以此多之也。

translations.literal: Feng was open and generous, slighting wealth and valuing righteousness. Whenever scholars in distress told him, he would pour out his resources to feed them; men of the realm therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was open and generous, slighting wealth and valuing righteousness. Whenever a scholar in distress came to him, he would pour out his resources to help; for this men of the realm held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 李愚，字子晦。

translations.literal: Li Yu, style Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, courtesy name Zihui.

sentences.zh: 自稱趙郡平棘西祖之後，家世為儒。

translations.literal: He claimed descent from the western ancestor of Pingji in Zhao Commandery; his family for generations were Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from the western branch of Pingji in Zhao Commandery, and his family had been Confucian scholars for generations.

sentences.zh: 父瞻業，應進士不第，遇亂，徙家渤海之無棣，以詩書訓子孫。

translations.literal: His father Zhanye sat for the jinshi examination but did not pass. Encountering disorder, he moved his family to Wudi in Bohai and instructed his descendants in poetry and the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhanye sat for the jinshi examination but failed. When turmoil came he moved the family to Wudi in Bohai and taught his descendants poetry and the classics.

sentences.zh: 愚童齔時，謹重有異常兒，年長方誌學，遍閱經史。

translations.literal: When Yu was still in childhood he was careful and grave beyond ordinary boys. When he grew older he set his mind on learning and read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a child Yu was careful and grave beyond ordinary boys. When he grew older he set his mind on learning and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 慕晏嬰之為人，初名晏平。

translations.literal: He admired the character of Yan Ying and at first was named Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: He admired the character of Yan Ying and at first bore the name Yanping.

sentences.zh: 為文尚氣格，有韓、柳體。

translations.literal: In writing he valued vigor and structure, in the manner of Han and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: In his writing he valued vigor and structure, in the manner of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 厲誌端莊，風神峻整，非禮不言，行不苟且。

translations.literal: He disciplined his will and was dignified; his bearing was stern and ordered. He did not speak outside ritual propriety and did not act carelessly.
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined his will and bore himself with dignity; his bearing was stern and ordered. He would not speak outside ritual propriety and would not act carelessly.

sentences.zh: 愚初以艱貧，求為假官，滄州盧彥威署安陵簿。

translations.literal: Yu at first, because of hardship and poverty, sought a provisional post; Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou appointed him recorder of Anling.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because of hardship and poverty, Yu sought a provisional post, and Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou appointed him recorder of Anling.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，服闋，隨計之長安。

translations.literal: He observed mourning; when the mourning period ended he went with the examination candidates to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After his period of mourning ended, he went with the examination candidates to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 屬關輔亂離，頻年罷舉，客於蒲、華之間。

translations.literal: The Guanzhong region was in turmoil and separation; examinations were suspended for years, and he sojourned between Pu and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzhong region was in turmoil and examinations were suspended for years, so he sojourned between Pu and Hua.

sentences.zh: 光化中，軍容劉季述、王奉先廢昭宗，立裕王，五月餘，諸侯無奔問者。

translations.literal: In Guanghua, Army Supervisor Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian deposed Zhaozong and enthroned Prince Yu. For more than five months no regional lord hurried to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guanghua era, army supervisors Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian deposed Zhaozong and enthroned Prince Yu. For more than five months no regional lord hurried to inquire after the emperor.

sentences.zh: 愚時在華陰，致書於華帥韓建，其略曰：「仆關東一布衣耳，幸讀書為文，每見君臣父子之際，有傷教害義之事，常痛心切齒，恨不得抽腸蹀血，肆之市朝。

translations.literal: Yu was then at Huayin and sent a letter to Hua commander Han Jian, in summary saying: "Your servant is but a commoner of the eastern passes, fortunate to read books and write. Whenever I see matters between ruler and minister, father and son, that injure teaching and harm righteousness, I am constantly pained to the marrow and grind my teeth, wishing I could tear out my entrails and trample blood, exposing them in the market and court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was then at Huayin and wrote to the Hua commander Han Jian, saying in summary, "Your servant is but a commoner of the eastern passes, fortunate enough to read and write. Whenever I see conduct between ruler and minister, father and son, that injures teaching and harms righteousness, I am heartsick and grind my teeth, wishing I could tear out my entrails and trample blood in the market and court.

sentences.zh: 明公居近關重鎮，君父幽辱月餘，坐視凶逆，而忘勤王之舉，仆所未喻也。

translations.literal: Your Excellency holds a weighty post near the pass. Ruler and father have been shamed in seclusion for more than a month, yet you sit watching the vicious rebels and forget the effort to restore the king—I cannot understand this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency holds a weighty post near the pass. Our ruler and father have been shamed in seclusion for more than a month, yet you sit watching vicious rebels and forget the effort to restore the throne—I cannot understand this.

sentences.zh: 仆竊計中朝輔弼，雖有誌而無權；

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that the central court's chief ministers, though they have will, have no power;
translations.idiomatic: I privately consider that the central court's chief ministers, though they have will, have no power;

sentences.zh: 外鎮諸侯，雖有權而無誌。

translations.literal: the frontier military governors, though they have power, have no will.
translations.idiomatic: the frontier military governors, though they have power, have no will.

sentences.zh: 惟明公忠義，社稷是依。

translations.literal: Only Your Excellency's loyalty and righteousness make you the state's reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Excellency's loyalty and righteousness make you the state's reliance.

sentences.zh: 往年車輅播遷，號泣奉迎，累歲供饋，再復朝廟，義感人心，至今歌詠。

translations.literal: In former years when the imperial carriage was driven about, you wept and welcomed it, for years supplied provisions, and restored the court and temple. Righteousness moved men's hearts and is sung to this day.
translations.idiomatic: In former years, when the imperial carriage was driven into exile, you wept and welcomed it back, supplied provisions for years, and restored the court and temple. Your righteousness moved men's hearts and is still sung today.

sentences.zh: 此時事勢，尤異於前，明公地處要衝，位兼將相，自宮闈變故，已涉旬時，若不號令率先，以圖反正，遲疑未決，一朝山東侯伯唱義連衡，鼓行而西，明公求欲自安，如何決策！

translations.literal: The situation at this time is especially different from before. Your Excellency stands at a strategic choke point and your position combines general and chief minister. Since the palace upheaval more than ten days have passed. If you do not take the lead with commands to plan restoration, and delay in indecision, one morning the lords of Shandong may raise righteous banners in alliance, beat drums and march west—how will Your Excellency seek your own safety, and what decision will you make!
translations.idiomatic: The situation now is especially different from before. Your Excellency stands at a strategic choke point and holds both military and civil authority. Since the palace upheaval more than ten days have passed. If you do not take the lead with commands to plan restoration, and delay in indecision, one morning the lords of Shandong may raise righteous banners in alliance and march west with drums beating—how will Your Excellency seek your own safety, and what decision will you make!

sentences.zh: 此必然之勢也。

translations.literal: This is the inevitable trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the inevitable trend.

sentences.zh: 不如馳檄四方，諭以逆順，軍聲一振，則元凶破膽，浹旬之間，二豎之首傳於天下，計無便於此者。

translations.literal: Better to dispatch proclamations to the four quarters, instructing them in rebellion and obedience. Once the army's fame resounds, the chief culprit will lose heart; within ten days the heads of the two villains may be transmitted through the realm. No plan is more advantageous than this.
translations.idiomatic: Better to dispatch proclamations to the four quarters, instructing them in rebellion and obedience. Once the army's fame resounds, the chief culprits will lose heart; within ten days the heads of the two villains may be transmitted through the realm. No plan is more advantageous than this.

sentences.zh: 」建深禮遇之，堅辭還山。

translations.literal: " Jian treated him with deep courtesy, but Yu firmly declined and returned to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian treated him with deep courtesy, but Yu firmly declined and returned to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 天復初，駕在鳳翔，汴軍攻蒲、華，愚避難東歸洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu the emperor was at Fengxiang; Bian armies attacked Pu and Hua. Yu fled east and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era the emperor was at Fengxiang while Bian armies attacked Pu and Hua. Yu fled east and returned to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時衛公李德裕孫延古在平泉舊墅，愚往依焉。

translations.literal: At the time Duke Wei Li Deyu's grandson Yangu was at the old estate at Pingquan; Yu went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Duke Wei Li Deyu's grandson Yangu was living at the old estate at Pingquan, and Yu went to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 子弟親采梠負薪，以給朝夕，未嘗幹人。

translations.literal: He and the younger men personally gathered firewood to supply day and night, and never sought favors from others.
translations.idiomatic: He and the younger men personally gathered firewood to supply their daily needs and never sought favors from others.

sentences.zh: 故少師薛廷珪掌貢籍之歲，登進士第；

translations.literal: In the year when former Junior Mentor Xue Tinggui managed the examination registry, he passed the jinshi examination;
translations.idiomatic: In the year when former junior mentor Xue Tinggui managed the examination registry, he passed the jinshi examination;

sentences.zh: 又登宏詞料，授河南府參軍，遂下居洛表白沙之別墅。

translations.literal: he also passed the Hongci examination and was appointed aide of Henan Prefecture, then went down to dwell at a villa at Baisha outside Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: he also passed the Hongci examination and was appointed aide of Henan Prefecture, then retired to a villa at Baisha outside Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 梁有禪代之謀，柳璨希旨殺害朝士，愚以衣冠自相殘害，乃避地河朔，與宗人李延光客於山東。

translations.literal: Liang had plans for usurping the mandate; Liu Can to please the throne killed court scholars. Yu, seeing the gentry destroy one another, fled to Heshuo and with his clansman Li Yanguang sojourned in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had plans to usurp the mandate, and Liu Can killed court scholars to please the throne. Seeing the gentry destroy one another, Yu fled to Heshuo and with his clansman Li Yanguang sojourned in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝嗣位，雅好儒士，延光素相款奉，得侍講禁中，屢言愚之行高學贍，有史魚、蘧瑗之風。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor of Liang succeeded, he greatly favored Confucian scholars. Yanguang had long been cordial with him and obtained a post lecturing within the palace, repeatedly speaking of Yu's lofty conduct and ample learning, with the air of Shiyu and Qu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the last emperor of Liang succeeded, he greatly favored Confucian scholars. Yanguang had long been cordial with him and obtained a post lecturing within the palace, repeatedly praising Yu's lofty conduct and ample learning, with the integrity of Shiyu and Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 召見，嗟賞久之，擢為左拾遺。

translations.literal: Yu was summoned for audience; the emperor sighed in admiration for a long time and promoted him to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was summoned for audience; the emperor sighed in admiration for a long time and promoted him to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 俄充崇政院直學士，或預谘謀，而儼然正色，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Soon he served as direct academician of the Chongzheng Hall, sometimes taking part in counsel, yet bearing himself with stern dignity and not fearing the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as direct academician of the Chongzheng Hall, sometimes taking part in counsel, yet bearing himself with stern dignity and not fearing the powerful.

sentences.zh: 衡王入朝，重臣李振輩皆致拜，惟愚長揖。

translations.literal: When Prince Heng entered court, heavy ministers such as Li Zhen all performed obeisance; only Yu gave a long bow with hands clasped.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Heng entered court, senior ministers such as Li Zhen all performed obeisance; only Yu gave a long bow with hands clasped.

sentences.zh: 末帝讓之曰：「衡王，朕之兄。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor reproached him: "Prince Heng is Our elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The last emperor reproached him: "Prince Heng is Our elder brother.

sentences.zh: 朕猶致拜，崇政使李振等皆拜，爾何傲耶！

translations.literal: Even We perform obeisance, and Chongzheng Commissioner Li Zhen and the rest all bow—why are you so arrogant!
translations.idiomatic: Even We perform obeisance, and Chongzheng Commissioner Li Zhen and the rest all bow—why are you so arrogant!

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下以家人禮兄，振等私臣也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your Majesty treats your brother with family courtesy. Zhen and the rest are Your private ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Your Majesty treats your brother with family courtesy. Zhen and the rest are Your private ministers.

sentences.zh: 臣居朝列，與王無素，安敢諂事。

translations.literal: Your servant stands in the court ranks and has no prior tie with the prince—how dare I fawn and serve.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant stands in the court ranks and has no prior tie with the prince—how dare I fawn and flatter.

sentences.zh: 」其剛毅如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his firmness.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his firmness.

sentences.zh: 晉州節度使華溫琪在任違法，籍民家財，其家訟於朝，製使劾之，伏罪。

translations.literal: Jinzhou military governor Hua Wenqi while in office violated the law and registered common people's family property. The family sued at court; the imperial commissioner impeached him and he confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinzhou military governor Hua Wenqi violated the law while in office and seized common people's family property. The family sued at court; the imperial commissioner impeached him and he confessed guilt.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝以先朝草昧之臣，不忍加法，愚堅按其罪。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang, because Wenqi was a minister from the founding days of hardship, was unwilling to apply the law. Yu firmly pressed the charge.
translations.idiomatic: The last emperor of Liang, because Wenqi was a minister from the founding days of hardship, was unwilling to apply the law. Yu firmly pressed the charge.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝詔曰：「朕若不與鞫窮，謂予不念赤子；

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang issued an edict: "If We do not investigate to the end, it will be said We do not care for Our children;
translations.idiomatic: The last emperor of Liang issued an edict: "If We do not investigate to the end, it will be said We do not care for Our children;

sentences.zh: 若或遂行典憲，謂予不念功臣。

translations.literal: if We then carry out the statutes, it will be said We do not care for meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: if We then carry out the statutes, it will be said We do not care for meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 為爾君者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: For one who is your lord—is it not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: For one who is your lord—is it not also difficult!

sentences.zh: 其華溫琪所受贓，宜官給代還所訟之家。

translations.literal: The bribes Hua Wenqi received should be supplied by the state and returned to the suing families.
translations.idiomatic: The bribes Hua Wenqi received should be supplied by the state and returned to the suing families.

sentences.zh: 」貞明中，通事舍人李霄傭夫毆僦舍人致死，法司案律，罪在李霄。

translations.literal: " In Zhenming, Courier Gentleman Li Xiao's hired laborer beat a lodger to death. The legal office applied the statutes and found guilt lay with Li Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Zhenming era, courier gentleman Li Xiao's hired laborer beat a lodger to death. The legal office applied the statutes and found guilt lay with Li Xiao.

sentences.zh: 愚白：「李霄手不鬥毆。

translations.literal: Yu stated: "Li Xiao's hand did not join in the beating.
translations.idiomatic: Yu stated, "Li Xiao's hand did not join in the beating.

sentences.zh: 庸夫致死，安得坐其主耶！

translations.literal: A common fellow caused death—how can his master be punished!
translations.idiomatic: A common fellow caused the death—how can his master be punished!

sentences.zh: 」以是忤旨。

translations.literal: " For this he offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: " For this he offended the imperial will.

sentences.zh: 愚自拾遺再遷膳部員外郎，賜緋，改司勳員外郎，賜紫，至是罷職，曆許、鄧觀察判官。

translations.literal: Yu rose from Reminder to Outside Regular of the Provisioners Section and was granted scarlet; was changed to Outside Regular of the Merit Section and granted purple. At this point he was dismissed and successively served as observation commissioner adjutant of Xu and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rose from reminder to outside regular of the provisioners section and was granted scarlet robes; was reassigned as outside regular of the merit section and granted purple robes. At this point he was dismissed and successively served as observation commissioner adjutant of Xu and Deng.

sentences.zh: 初在內職，慈州舉子張礪依焉。

translations.literal: When he first held an inner court post, Cizhou examination candidate Zhang Li relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first held an inner court post, the Cizhou examination candidate Zhang Li relied on him.

sentences.zh: 貞明中，礪自河陽北歸莊宗，補授太原府掾，出入崇闥之間，揄揚愚之節概，及言愚之所為文《仲尼遇》、《顏回壽》、《夷齊非餓人》等篇，北人望風稱之。

translations.literal: In Zhenming, Li returned north from Heyang to Zhuangzong, was appointed supplement clerk of Taiyuan Prefecture, and moving in and out of the inner gates praised Yu's integrity and spoke of Yu's writings such as "Confucius Encounters," "Yan Hui's Longevity," and "Boyi and Shuqi Were Not Starving Men." Northerners heard of him and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming era, Li returned north from Heyang to Zhuangzong, was appointed supplement clerk of Taiyuan Prefecture, and moving in and out of the inner gates praised Yu's integrity and spoke of Yu's writings such as "Confucius Encounters," "Yan Hui's Longevity," and "Boyi and Shuqi Were Not Starving Men." Northerners heard of him and praised him.

sentences.zh: 洎莊宗都洛陽，鄧帥俾奏章入朝，諸貴見之，禮接如舊。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong made Luoyang his capital, the Deng commander had a memorial submitted to court. The nobles on seeing him received him with courtesy as of old.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong made Luoyang his capital, the Deng commander had a memorial submitted to court on Yu's behalf. The nobles, on seeing him, received him with courtesy as of old.

sentences.zh: 尋為主客郎中，數月，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Director of the Host-Guest Bureau; after several months he was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made director of the host-guest bureau, and after several months he was summoned as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，魏王繼岌征蜀，請為都統判官，仍帶本職從軍。

translations.literal: In the third year Prince Ji of Wei campaigned against Shu; Yu requested to serve as adjutant to the commander-in-chief, still holding his original post while following the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Prince Ji of Wei campaigned against Shu, Yu asked to serve as adjutant to the commander-in-chief, retaining his original post while accompanying the army.

sentences.zh: 時物議以蜀險阻，未可長驅，郭崇韜問計於愚，愚曰：「如聞蜀人厭其主荒恣，倉卒必不為用。

translations.literal: At the time public opinion held that Shu was rugged and dangerous and could not be overrun in a long drive. Guo Chongtao asked Yu for a plan. Yu said: "As I hear, the people of Shu loathe their ruler's dissipation and excess; in haste he surely cannot make use of them.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Shu was rugged and dangerous and that a long drive was impossible. Guo Chongtao asked Yu for counsel. Yu said, "As I hear, the people of Shu loathe their ruler's dissipation and excess; in haste he surely cannot make use of them.

sentences.zh: 宜乘其人二三，風馳電擊，彼必破膽，安能守險。

translations.literal: We should take advantage when his men are divided two or three ways, strike like wind and lightning, and they will surely lose heart—how can they hold the passes?
translations.idiomatic: We should strike when his men are divided, move like wind and lightning, and they will surely lose heart—how can they hold the passes?

sentences.zh: 」及前軍至固鎮，收軍食十五萬斛，崇韜喜，謂愚曰：「公能料事，吾軍濟矣！

translations.literal: " When the vanguard reached Guzhen and collected one hundred fifty thousand hu of army grain, Chongtao was pleased and said to Yu: "You can foresee affairs—our army is saved!
translations.idiomatic: " When the vanguard reached Guzhen and collected one hundred fifty thousand hu of army grain, Chongtao was pleased and said to Yu, "You can foresee affairs—our army is saved!

sentences.zh: 」招討判官陳乂至寶雞，稱疾乞留在後。

translations.literal: " Pacification adjutant Chen Yi reached Baoji and claimed illness, asking to remain in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: " The pacification adjutant Chen Yi reached Baoji and claimed illness, asking to remain in the rear.

sentences.zh: 愚厲聲曰：「陳乂見利則進，懼難則止。

translations.literal: Yu said in a harsh voice: "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he fears difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said in a harsh voice, "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he fears difficulty.

sentences.zh: 今大軍涉險，人心易惑，正可斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Now the great army crosses danger and men's hearts are easily unsettled—he should be beheaded to warn the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great army crosses danger and men's hearts are easily unsettled—he should be beheaded to warn the ranks.

sentences.zh: 」由是軍人無遲留者。

translations.literal: " From this there were no soldiers who lingered.
translations.idiomatic: " From this onward no soldier dared linger.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍書羽檄，皆出其手。

translations.literal: At this time military documents and urgent proclamations all came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: At this time military documents and urgent proclamations all came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，就拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was appointed Secretariat Drafter on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, he was appointed secretariat drafter on the spot.

sentences.zh: 師還，明宗即位。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Mingzong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Mingzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 時西征副招討使任圜為宰相，雅相欽重，屢言於安重誨，請引為同列；

translations.literal: At the time Western Campaign Deputy Pacification Commissioner Ren Huan was chief minister and greatly esteemed Yu, repeatedly speaking to An Chonghui and asking to bring him into the same rank;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the western campaign deputy pacification commissioner Ren Huan was chief minister and greatly esteemed Yu, repeatedly asking An Chonghui to bring him into the council;

sentences.zh: 屬孔循用事，援引崔協以塞其請。

translations.literal: but Kong Xun held power and brought in Cui Xie to block the request.
translations.idiomatic: but Kong Xun held power and brought in Cui Xie to block the request.

sentences.zh: 俄以本職權知貢舉，改兵部侍郎，充翰林承旨。

translations.literal: Soon in his original post he acted as commissioner for the examinations; he was changed to Vice Minister of War and served as Hanlin Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he acted as commissioner for the examinations in his original post, was reassigned as vice minister of war, and served as Hanlin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長興初，除太常卿，屬趙鳳出鎮邢台，乃拜中書侍郎、平章事，轉集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing he was made Minister of Ceremonies. When Zhao Feng went out to govern Xingtai, Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, then transferred to Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing era he was made minister of ceremonies. When Zhao Feng went out to govern Xingtai, Yu was appointed vice director of the secretariat and grand councilor, then transferred to grand academician of the Jixian Hall.

sentences.zh: 長興季年，秦王恣橫，權要之臣，避禍不暇，邦之存亡，無敢言者。

translations.literal: In the last years of Changxing, Prince of Qin acted with reckless license. Powerful ministers had no leisure to avoid disaster; on the state's survival or destruction, none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Changxing, the Prince of Qin acted with reckless license. Powerful ministers had no leisure to avoid disaster, and on the state's survival or destruction none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 愚性剛介，往往形言，然人無唱和者。

translations.literal: Yu was firm and upright by nature and often spoke out plainly, yet no one echoed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was firm and upright by nature and often spoke out plainly, yet no one echoed him.

sentences.zh: 後轉門下侍郎，監修國史，兼吏部尚書，與諸儒修成《創業功臣傳》三十卷。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery, supervised compilation of the national history, and concurrently held Minister of Personnel. With various scholars he completed the thirty-juan Biographies of Founding Merit Holders.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to vice director of the chancellery, supervised compilation of the national history, and concurrently served as minister of personnel. With various scholars he completed the thirty-juan 《Biographies of Founding Merit Holders》.

sentences.zh: 愚初不治第，既命為相，官借延賓館居之。

translations.literal: Yu at first did not build a mansion. Once appointed chief minister, the government lent him the Guest Reception Hall to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Yu at first did not build a mansion. Once appointed chief minister, the government lent him the guest reception hall to dwell in.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，詔近臣宣諭，延之中堂，設席惟筦秸，使人言之，明宗特賜帷帳茵褥。

translations.literal: Once when he was ill, an edict ordered a nearby minister to convey imperial concern. He received the envoy in the central hall and set out only matting of reeds, which the envoy reported. Mingzong specially granted curtains, screens, and bedding.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he was ill, an edict ordered a nearby minister to convey imperial concern. He received the envoy in the central hall with only reed matting for seating, which the envoy reported. Mingzong specially granted curtains, screens, and bedding.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note:

sentences.zh: （《職官分紀》云：長興四年，愚病，明宗遣中使宣問。

translations.literal: (The Zhiguan Fenji says: In the fourth year of Changxing, Yu was ill and Mingzong sent a palace envoy to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zhiguan Fenji》 says: In the fourth year of Changxing, Yu was ill and Mingzong sent a palace envoy to inquire.

sentences.zh: 愚所居寢室，蕭然四壁，病榻弊氈而已。

translations.literal: Yu's sleeping chamber was bare on four walls, with only a sick couch and worn rug.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's sleeping chamber was bare on four walls, with only a sick couch and a worn rug.

sentences.zh: 中使具言其事，帝曰：「宰相月俸幾何？

translations.literal: The palace envoy fully reported the matter. The emperor said: "How much is a chief minister's monthly salary?
translations.idiomatic: The palace envoy fully reported the matter. The emperor said, "How much is a chief minister's monthly salary?

sentences.zh: 而委頓如此。

translations.literal: Yet he is so exhausted and worn.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is so exhausted and worn.

sentences.zh: 」詔賜絹百匹、錢百千、帷帳什物一十三事。）〉

translations.literal: " An edict granted one hundred bolts of silk, a hundred thousand cash, and thirteen kinds of curtains, screens, and furnishings.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " An edict granted one hundred bolts of silk, a hundred thousand cash, and thirteen kinds of curtains, screens, and furnishings.)〉

sentences.zh: 閔帝嗣位，誌修德政，易月之制才除，便延訪學士讀《貞觀政要》、《太宗實錄》，有意於致理。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, he resolved to cultivate virtuous government. The mourning period had barely ended when he summoned academicians to read the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Era and the Veritable Records of Taizong, intending to bring order to rule.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min succeeded, he resolved to cultivate virtuous government. The mourning period had barely ended when he summoned academicians to read the 《Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Era》 and the 《Veritable Records of Taizong》, intending to bring order to rule.

sentences.zh: 愚私謂同列曰：「吾君延訪，少及吾輩，位高責重，事亦堪憂，奈宗社何！

translations.literal: Yu privately said to his colleagues: "Our lord in his audiences seldom reaches us. Our positions are high and our responsibilities heavy—the matter is also worrisome. What will become of the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Yu privately said to his colleagues, "Our lord in his audiences seldom reaches us. Our positions are high and our responsibilities heavy—the matter is also worrisome. What will become of the altars of state!

sentences.zh: 」皆惕息而不敢言。

translations.literal: " All held their breath in fear and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " All held their breath in fear and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 以恩例進位左僕射。

translations.literal: By favor he was advanced to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: By favor he was advanced to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，徽陵禮畢，馮道出鎮同州，愚加特進、太微宮使、宏文館大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, when the Huiling rites were complete, Feng Dao went out to govern Tongzhou. Yu was given Special Advancement, Commissioner of the Taiwei Palace, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qingtai, when the Huiling rites were complete, Feng Dao went out to govern Tongzhou. Yu was given special advancement, commissioner of the Taiwei Palace, and grand academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 宰相劉句與馮道為婚家，道既出鎮，兩人在中書，或舊事不便要厘革者，對論不定。

translations.literal: Chief minister Liu Gou and Feng Dao were related by marriage. Once Dao had gone out to govern, the two men were in the Secretariat; on old matters inconvenient to reform, they debated face to face without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Liu Gou and Feng Dao were related by marriage. Once Dao had gone out to govern, the two men remained in the secretariat; on old matters inconvenient to reform, they debated face to face without resolution.

sentences.zh: 愚性太峻，因曰：「此事賢家翁所為，更之不亦便乎！

translations.literal: Yu was excessively stern by nature and therefore said: "This matter was done by your worthy father-in-law—would it not be more convenient to change it!
translations.idiomatic: Yu was excessively stern by nature and said, "This matter was done by your worthy father-in-law—would it not be more convenient to change it!

sentences.zh: 」句憾其言切，於是每言必相折難，或至喧呼。

translations.literal: " Gou resented his cutting words; from then on whenever they spoke they inevitably refuted each other, sometimes even shouting.
translations.idiomatic: " Gou resented his cutting words; from then on whenever they spoke they inevitably refuted each other, sometimes even shouting.

sentences.zh: 無幾，兩人俱罷相守本官。

translations.literal: Before long both men were dismissed and kept their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both men were dismissed and kept their original posts.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年秋，愚已嬰疾，率多請告，累表乞骸，不允，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Qingtai, Yu was already afflicted with illness, mostly requesting leave, and repeatedly submitted memorials asking to retire; this was not granted, and he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Qingtai, Yu was already gravely ill, mostly requesting leave, and repeatedly submitted memorials asking to retire; this was not granted, and he died in office.

sentences.zh: 任圜，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Ren Huan was a man of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖清，成都少尹。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qing was Vice Governor of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qing was vice governor of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 父茂宏，避地太原，奏授西河令；

translations.literal: His father Maohong fled to Taiyuan and was memorialized for appointment as magistrate of Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: His father Maohong fled to Taiyuan and was memorialized for appointment as magistrate of Xihe;

sentences.zh: 有子五人，曰圖、回、圜、團、冏，風彩俱異。

translations.literal: he had five sons named Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong, each with a distinctive bearing.
translations.idiomatic: he had five sons named Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong, each with a distinctive bearing.

sentences.zh: 武皇愛之，以宗女妻團，歷代、憲二郡刺史。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor favored them; he married a clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor favored them; he married a clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian commanderies.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭典兵於晉陽，與圜遊處甚洽，及鎮澤潞，請為觀察支使，解褐，賜朱紱。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao commanded troops at Jinyang and was on very friendly terms with Huan in their companionship. When he governed Ze-Lu, he requested Huan as observation administrative aide. Huan left the commoner's garb and was granted scarlet sash.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao commanded troops at Jinyang and was on very friendly terms with Huan. When Sizhao governed Ze-Lu, he requested Huan as observation administrative aide. Huan left the commoner's garb and was granted a scarlet sash.

sentences.zh: 圜美姿容，有口辯。

translations.literal: Huan had handsome features and eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had handsome features and was eloquent.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭為人間諜於莊宗，方有微隙，圜奉使往來，常申理之，克成友於之道，圜之力也。

translations.literal: Sizhao served as an intermediary spy for Zhuangzong; when there was a slight rift, Huan went back and forth as envoy and often explained matters, achieving brotherly harmony—this was Huan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao served as an intermediary for Zhuangzong; when there was a slight rift, Huan went back and forth as envoy and often explained matters, achieving brotherly harmony—this was Huan's doing.

sentences.zh: 及丁母憂，莊宗承製起復潞州觀察判官，賜紫。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, Zhuangzong by imperial order recalled him from mourning as Ze-Lu observation adjutant and granted purple.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his mother, Zhuangzong by imperial order recalled him from mourning as Ze-Lu observation adjutant and granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 常山之役，嗣昭為帥，卒於軍，圜代總其事，號令如一，敵人不知。

translations.literal: In the Changshan campaign Sizhao was commander and died in the army. Huan took over all affairs; commands were as one, and the enemy did not know.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changshan campaign Sizhao was commander and died in the army. Huan took over all affairs; commands continued unchanged, and the enemy did not know.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞之，倍加獎賞。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard of this and doubled his rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong heard of this and doubled his rewards.

sentences.zh: 是秋，復以上黨之師攻常山，城中萬人突出，大將孫文進死之，賊逼我軍，圜麾騎士擊之，頗有殺獲。

translations.literal: That autumn he again led the Shangdang army to attack Changshan. Ten thousand men sallied from the city; great general Sun Wenjin died. The rebels pressed our army; Huan commanded horsemen to strike them and killed and captured many.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he again led the Shangdang army to attack Changshan. Ten thousand men sallied from the city; the great general Sun Wenjin was killed. The rebels pressed our army; Huan commanded horsemen to strike them and killed and captured many.

sentences.zh: 嘗以禍福諭其城中，鎮人信之，使乞降。

translations.literal: He once instructed the city on fortune and disaster; the people of Zhen believed him and sent someone to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He once instructed the city on fortune and disaster; the people of Zhen believed him and sent someone to beg surrender.

sentences.zh: 及城潰，誅元惡之外，官吏鹹保其家屬，亦圜所庇護焉。

translations.literal: When the city fell, beyond executing the chief culprits, officials and clerks all preserved their families—this too was under Huan's protection.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, beyond executing the chief culprits, officials and clerks all preserved their families—this too was under Huan's protection.

sentences.zh: 莊宗改鎮州為北京，以圜為工部尚書兼真定尹、北京副留守，行留守事。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong changed Zhenzhou to Northern Capital and appointed Huan Minister of Works and concurrently Governor of Zhending, Northern Capital Vice Regent, acting regent's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong changed Zhenzhou to the Northern Capital and appointed Huan minister of works and concurrently governor of Zhending, Northern Capital vice regent, acting in the regent's affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，郭崇韜兼鎮，改行軍司馬，充北面水陸轉運使，仍知府事。

translations.literal: The next year Guo Chongtao also held the command; Huan was changed to campaigning marshal, served as northern land-and-water transport commissioner, and still managed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Guo Chongtao also held the command; Huan was changed to campaigning marshal, served as northern land-and-water transport commissioner, and still managed prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，歸朝，守工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he returned to court and held the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang he returned to court and held the post of minister of works.

sentences.zh: 崇韜伐蜀，奏令從征，西蜀平，署圜黔南節度使，懇辭遂止。

translations.literal: When Chongtao campaigned against Shu he memorialized that Huan should follow the campaign. When Western Shu was pacified he appointed Huan military governor of Qiannan; Huan earnestly declined and it stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao campaigned against Shu he memorialized that Huan should follow the campaign. When Western Shu was pacified he appointed Huan military governor of Qiannan; Huan earnestly declined and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 魏王班師，行及利州，康延孝叛，以勁兵八千回劫西川。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wei withdrew the army and reached Lizhou, Kang Yanxiao rebelled and with eight thousand crack troops turned back to raid Western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei withdrew the army and reached Lizhou, Kang Yanxiao rebelled and with eight thousand crack troops turned back to raid Western Shu.

sentences.zh: 繼岌聞之，夜半命中使李廷安召圜，圜方寢，廷安登其床以告之，圜衣不及帶，遽見繼岌。

translations.literal: Jiji heard of it and at midnight ordered palace envoy Li Ting'an to summon Huan. Huan was just asleep; Ting'an climbed onto his bed to tell him. Huan had no time to belt his robe and hurried to see Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji heard of it and at midnight ordered the palace envoy Li Ting'an to summon Huan. Huan was asleep; Ting'an climbed onto his bed to tell him. Huan had no time to belt his robe and hurried to see Jiji.

sentences.zh: 繼岌泣而言曰：「紹琛負恩，非尚書不能制。

translations.literal: Jiji weeping said: "Shaochen has betrayed grace—only the Minister can control him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji wept and said, "Shaochen has betrayed us—only you, Minister, can control him.

sentences.zh: 」即署圜為招討副使，與都指揮使梁漢顒等率兵攻延孝於漢州，擒之。

translations.literal: " He at once appointed Huan deputy pacification commissioner; with Commander-in-Chief Liang Hanyong and others he led troops to attack Yanxiao at Hanzhou and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once appointed Huan deputy pacification commissioner; with the commander-in-chief Liang Hanyong and others he led troops to attack Yanxiao at Hanzhou and captured him.

sentences.zh: 旋至渭南，繼岌遇害。

translations.literal: Soon they reached Weinan; Jiji was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they reached Weinan, where Jiji was murdered.

sentences.zh: 圜代總全師，朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: Huan took command of the entire army and presented himself at court in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan took command of the entire army and presented himself at court in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘉其功，拜平章事，判三司。

translations.literal: Mingzong praised his merit and appointed him Grand Councilor, with charge of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong praised his merit and appointed him grand councilor, with charge of the three offices.

sentences.zh: 圜揀拔賢俊，杜絕幸門，百官俸入為孔謙減折。

translations.literal: Huan selected worthy and talented men and blocked the gate of favor; officials' salaries had been reduced and discounted by Kong Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Huan selected worthy and talented men and blocked the gate of favor; officials' salaries had been reduced and discounted by Kong Qian.

sentences.zh: 圜以廷臣為國家羽儀，故優假班行，禁其虛估，期月之內，府庫充贍，朝廷修葺，軍民鹹足。

translations.literal: Huan held that court ministers were the state's ceremonial plumes and banners, so he granted favorable treatment to the official ranks and forbade false valuation. Within a month the treasury was full, the court was repaired, and army and people were all provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Huan held that court ministers were the state's ceremonial plumes and banners, so he granted favorable treatment to the official ranks and forbade false valuation. Within a month the treasury was full, the court was repaired, and army and people were all provided for.

sentences.zh: 雖憂國如家，而切於功名，故為安重誨所忌。

translations.literal: Though he grieved for the state as for his own family, he was keen on fame and achievement, and therefore was resented by An Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Though he grieved for the state as for his own family, he was keen on fame and achievement, and therefore was resented by An Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 嘗與重誨會於私第，有妓善歌，重誨求之不得，嫌隙自茲而深矣。

translations.literal: Once he met Chonghui at a private residence. There was a singing girl skilled in song; Chonghui asked for her but could not obtain her, and enmity from this grew deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met Chonghui at a private residence. There was a singing girl skilled in song; Chonghui asked for her but could not obtain her, and enmity from this grew deep.

sentences.zh: 先是，使人食券，皆出於戶部，重誨止之，俾須內出，爭於御前，往復數四，竟為所沮，

translations.literal: Earlier, envoys' food vouchers all came from the Ministry of Revenue. Chonghui stopped this and made them require inner-court issuance. They disputed before the throne, back and forth several times, and in the end were blocked by him,
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, envoys' food vouchers all came from the Ministry of Revenue. Chonghui stopped this and required inner-court issuance instead. They disputed before the throne, back and forth several times, and in the end were blocked by him,

sentences.zh: 上退朝，宮人問上：「適與重誨論事為誰？

translations.literal: When the emperor left court, a palace woman asked: "With whom was Your Majesty just now discussing affairs with Chonghui?
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor left court, a palace woman asked, "With whom was Your Majesty just now discussing affairs with Chonghui?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「宰相。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The chief minister.

sentences.zh: 」宮人曰：「妾在長安宮中，未嘗見宰相、樞密奏事敢如是者，蓋輕大家耳！

translations.literal: " The palace woman said: "When your servant was in the Chang'an palace, I never saw a chief minister or privy councilor report affairs dare to be like this—they must look down on the great house!
translations.idiomatic: " The palace woman said, "When I was in the Chang'an palace, I never saw a chief minister or privy councilor report affairs dare to be like this—they must look down on the imperial house!

sentences.zh: 因求罷三司。

translations.literal: Huan therefore asked to resign the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Huan therefore asked to resign charge of the three offices.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，除太子少保致仕，出居磁州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired, going out to dwell in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made junior mentor of the heir apparent and retired, going out to dwell in Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 及朱守殷叛，重誨乘間誣其結構，立遣人稱製就害之，乃下詔曰：「太子少保致仕任圜，早推勳舊，曾委重難，既退免於劇權，俾優閑於外地，而乃不遵禮分，潛附守殷，緘題罔避於嫌疑，情旨頗彰於怨望。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled, Chonghui seized the opportunity to accuse him of conspiracy and at once sent a man bearing an imperial order to kill him on the spot. An edict was then issued: "Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, retired Ren Huan, was early esteemed as an old merit holder and once entrusted with weighty difficulty. Having retired from intense power, he was granted ease in an outer region—yet he did not observe ritual propriety, secretly attached himself to Shouyin, sealed letters without avoiding suspicion, and his sentiments clearly showed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled, Chonghui seized the opportunity to accuse him of conspiracy and at once sent a man bearing an imperial order to kill him on the spot. An edict was then issued: "The retired junior mentor of the heir apparent Ren Huan was early esteemed as an old merit holder and once entrusted with weighty responsibility. Having retired from intense power, he was granted ease in an outer region—yet he did not observe ritual propriety, secretly attached himself to Shouyin, sealed letters without avoiding suspicion, and his sentiments clearly showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 自收汴壘，備見蹤由，若務含宏，是孤典憲，尚全大體，止罪一身。

translations.literal: Since the Bian stronghold was taken, his tracks have been fully seen. If We sought forbearance, We would betray the statutes; yet in preserving the larger frame, We punish only one man.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Bian stronghold was taken, his tracks have been fully seen. If We sought forbearance, We would betray the statutes; yet in preserving the larger frame, We punish only one man.

sentences.zh: 宜令本州於私第賜自盡。

translations.literal: Let this prefecture at his private residence grant him suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Let the local prefecture grant him suicide at his private residence.

sentences.zh: 」圜受命之日，聚族酣飲，神情不撓。

translations.literal: " On the day Huan received the order, he gathered his clan for hearty drinking; his spirit was unshaken.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day Huan received the order, he gathered his clan for hearty drinking; his spirit was unshaken.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，製贈太傅。

translations.literal: In Qingtai, by edict he was posthumously awarded Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era, by edict he was posthumously awarded grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 子徹，仕皇朝，位至度支郎中，卒。

translations.literal: His son Che served the imperial court, reaching Director of the Expenditure Section, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che served the imperial court, reaching director of the expenditure section, and died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：革、說承舊族之胄，佐新造之邦，業雖謝於財成，罪未聞於昭著，而乃為權臣之所忌，顧後命以無逃，靜而言之，亦可憫也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Ge and Shuo inherited the pedigrees of old clans and assisted a newly founded state. Their achievements, though short of completion, had crimes not heard to be conspicuous—yet they were resented by powerful ministers and looked to later fate without escape. Spoken calmly, this too is pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Ge and Shuo inherited the pedigrees of old clans and assisted a newly founded state. Their achievements, though short of completion, had no conspicuous crimes—yet they were resented by powerful ministers and could not escape their fate. Spoken calmly, this too is pitiable.

sentences.zh: 盧程器狹如是，形渥攸宜。

translations.literal: That Lu Cheng's capacity was so narrow—his punishment was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: That Lu Cheng's capacity was so narrow—his punishment was fitting.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳、李愚，咸以文學之名，俱踐岩廊之位，校其貞節，愚復優焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng and Li Yu both bore literary fame and together reached the hall of state on the cliff. Comparing their integrity, Yu was again superior.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng and Li Yu both bore literary fame and together reached the highest council. Comparing their integrity, Yu was again superior.

sentences.zh: 任圜有縱橫濟物之才，無明哲保身之道，退猶不免，籲可悲哉！

translations.literal: Ren Huan had talent to traverse and aid the realm but lacked the way of the wise to preserve himself; even in retirement he could not escape—alas, how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan had talent to traverse and aid the realm but lacked the way of the wise to preserve himself; even in retirement he could not escape—alas, how lamentable!
